chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Hibbler's popularity wanes; Australia tour with Hawkins, Wilson and Sarah
summary: Around 1960 bookings thin out, but they join a huge Australian tour in stadiums.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: There was a lot of fun and everything that I had with Al -- a lot of things. But anyway, that began to sort of wane, his popularity... A lot of things that he began to do wasn't very good for his career. Finally, about 1960, we began to do spotted engagements, one here, one there, we'd do three weeks here, we'd do a month here.

One time we did a trip to Australia, which was a very nice thing. I think this was in the early 60's. We went down to Australia, and there was a nice tour with Coleman Hawkins, the Teddy Wilson Trio with the bassist Arvell Shaw -- I've forgotten who the drummer was with Teddy Wilson. It also included Sarah Vaughan and her trio. Also, Dakota Staton... It was just a mammoth show. We played about three or four cities in Australia. And we played in these big stadiums, I guess they were soccer stadiums or something -- big stadiums and halls and places where they were huge and accommodated a large amount of people.
But as I said before, Al's thing began to wane. It got so whenever he had an engagement, he would call me, and I would go with him if I wasn't doing anything else.
